# Ubik

> Ubik is a decision intelligence workspace for frozen food trade operators, starting with importers, exporters and processors.

Ubik connects to email, WhatsApp, ERP, CRM, documents, meetings and market intelligence sources, then runs memory workflows and agents for trade operations.

## Core positioning

- Decision intelligence workspace for perishable trade
- Built for frozen food importers, exporters and processors
- Combines web workspace, local desktop context, memory workflows, market intelligence and enterprise-grade automation
- Designed for RFQ-to-quote, PO ingestion, VMI, margin protection, traceability and operational intelligence
- Built by operators from frozen food, supply chain and AI-native product teams

## Product

- Base: personal AI workspace for operators, with Ubik Webapp and Ubik Local included
- Enterprise: custom workflow automation for teams, with domain expert and forward-deployed product engineer support
- Ubik Local: included desktop add-on for local meeting recording and, later, hotkey-summoned desktop context bridging
- Supports 10+ LLMs including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok and more
- Supports private, local and air-gapped deployments for enterprise customers
- Integrates with email, WhatsApp, ERP, CRM, documents, spreadsheets, meetings and market intelligence tools

## Buyers

Ubik is for frozen food importers, exporters and processors who manage trade across email, WhatsApp, spreadsheets, ERP and CRM systems.

Primary ICP:
- $25Mn+ customer aggregate revenue proof point
- 100+ containers per year
- Teams where inboxes and WhatsApp threads act like the real ERP
- Operators who need faster quotes, cleaner PO processing, margin visibility and traceability

## Outcomes

- Faster RFQ-to-quote workflows
- Cleaner PO extraction and ERP handoff
- Live market intelligence and import/export project tracking
- Compounding memory across inbox, meetings, projects and trade artifacts
- Lower operational leakage from slow decisions and fragmented context

## Ubik Local

Ubik Local is included with Base and Enterprise. Today, it records and summarizes local meetings. Over time, it becomes the desktop context bridge for Ubik: a lightweight, hotkey-summoned overlay that connects local context, meetings, browser activity and the Ubik Webapp.

## Security and data handling

Ubik minimizes what is shared with external LLMs. Models are used for planning, reasoning and drafting actions, not for bulk raw-data ingestion. Sensitive data can remain in Ubik's context layer, local workspace or private deployment depending on the customer setup. Customer data is not used to train third-party models.

## Trade Notes

### The Invisible Drift

Path: /blog/ai-monitor-layer-seafood-trade

Summary: An operational AI case study showing why seafood teams need a monitor layer before LLM output becomes workflow state. It uses a 735-row seafood exhibitor country-attribution task and a 662-row matched A/B comparison to explain evidence capture, disagreement detection, confidence routing, green/amber/red review queues, and human escalation.

Key terms: seafood AI monitoring, LLM disagreement, evidence routing, AI governance in workflows, country attribution, supplier intelligence, model evaluation, Arena leaderboard, perishable trade AI.

### The 60-bps Bleed

Path: /blog/the-60-bps-bleed-shrimp-margin-loss

Summary: A visual seafood margin note showing how an apparently clean shrimp RFQ-to-PO cycle can leak 60 basis points through quote latency, counterparty scoring gaps, FX timing, freight drift, demurrage and detention, temperature deviation, count-size slippage, deglazed-weight economics, forwarder spread, working-capital carry and unclaimed remission.

Key terms: shrimp margin leakage, seafood RFQ workflow, deglazed weight, demurrage detention, AD CVD reserve, seafood trade finance, free-time burn-down, perishable trade AI.

### Origin Roulette 2026

Path: /blog/origin-roulette-2026-shrimp-sourcing

Summary: A shrimp buyer strategy note for Q3 2026 and Q1 2027 forward books. It compares Ecuador, India, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, China, Saudi Arabia and Bangladesh across landed-duty stack exposure, AD/CVD risk, EU wild-caught CATCH / Annex IV scope, FDA import certification, value-added processing capability, halal positioning and origin diversification.

Key terms: shrimp sourcing strategy, warm-water shrimp tariffs, seafood buyer strategy, Ecuador shrimp exports, India shrimp EU FTA, Vietnam shrimp re-export, Indonesia shrimp FDA certification, Saudi shrimp halal, perishable trade AI.
